title: AG’s office seeks consumer protections following AI startup bankruptcy
key_facts: Colorado is leading a coalition of state attorneys general seeking protections for consumer data in the bankruptcy proceedings of Character.AI.
The states recommended privacy and safety protections for any sale or transfer of the company's business or assets.
Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 earlier this week; launched in 2021, it lets users chat with customizable characters.
Before filing, Character.AI agreed that Disney would be stalking horse bidder to license some of its intellectual property, according to CNBC.
Several states, including Colorado, investigated the company after a 2024 wrongful-death lawsuit over a 14-year-old boy in Florida.
Colorado passed House Bill 1263 last session regulating AI chatbot companies, including disclosure to minors.
quote_evidence: Colorado is leading a coalition seeking protections of consumer data in bankruptcy proceedings of an artificial intelligence chatbot company.
Character.ai filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy earlier this week.
why_it_matters_hint: Chatbot users' sensitive data could be sold in a bankruptcy.
